key_insight: Exactly compressed unary circuits resolve bosonic tunneling on IBM and IonQ hardware, while much deeper binary product-formula circuits fail to reproduce the transfer.
engineering_relevance: Encoding and circuit compilation jointly determine hardware feasibility, so qubit savings must be weighed against two-qubit gate depth.
method: Compare binary and unary position-lattice encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors.
Implement binary kinetic evolution with a quantum Fourier transform and unary evolution with excitation-conserving exchange gates.
Exploit the single-degree-of-freedom free-fermion structure to compress unary dynamics exactly into fixed-size nearest-neighbor circuits.
evidence_signal: With about 200 two-qubit gates, unary circuits reduce right-well probability from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and from 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ; binary circuits using several thousand gates do not reproduce the transfer.
watch_item: Unary encoding requires one qubit per lattice site, and inter-register interactions in coupled oscillators prevent this exact compression, making encoding choice dependent on grid size and evolution time.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics with binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors
